stories.headline: Anthropic flies senior staff to DC to repair Mythos 5 and Fable 5 export-control dispute with White House

key_facts.fact: Senior technical staff from Anthropic are in Washington to meet with White House officials and try to resolve the dispute that took the company's Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models offline.
key_facts.excerpt: Senior technical Anthropic staff are in Washington to meet with White House officials to try to fix a dispute that has taken Anthropic's most advanced models offline.

key_facts.fact: A Trump administration official tells Fox Business the export controls were triggered by Anthropic's 'recklessness' in responding to issues with its latest release.
key_facts.excerpt: A senior Trump administration official tells FOX Business that Anthropic's 'recklessness' in responding to issues with the company's latest artificial intelligence release led to export controls.

key_facts.fact: Officials say Amazon AI experts orchestrated a jailbreak on Fable 5 after its June 9 release, opening the full cyber abilities of Mythos 5, the more advanced model in the family.
key_facts.excerpt: Administration officials say the concerns were realized last week when Amazon AI experts were able to orchestrate a 'jailbreak' on Fable 5 after it was released on June 9 alongside Mythos 5, the latter of which was only released to a limited group.

key_facts.fact: A source close to Anthropic says the initial government call gave no technical details, only a request to pull Fable 5 within 90 minutes, and that CEO Dario Amodei has been engaged from the beginning and remains eager to resolve any concerns.
key_facts.excerpt: A source close to Anthropic says there were no details in the initial call with government officials, just a request to pull down the Fable 5 model within 90 minutes. The source adds that Amodei and other senior staff have been engaged from the beginning, there was no refusal to fix an issue and the company remains eager to resolve any concerns.

key_facts.fact: A Fortune report on June 14 says Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's warning to the White House, plus concerns about unauthorized Chinese access and cybersecurity fears, led the administration to cut off foreign access to Fable 5.
key_facts.excerpt: A warning from Amazon chief executive Andy Jassy, concerns about unauthorized Chinese access, and cybersecurity fears all reportedly led the Trump administration to cut off foreign access to Anthropic's powerful new AI model, Fable 5.

stories.headline: 40+ cybersecurity leaders urge Trump to restore Anthropic Mythos 5 and Fable 5 access

key_facts.fact: Prominent cybersecurity leaders, including CISOs and executives at Adobe, Zoom and Sophos, are urging the Trump administration to reverse restrictions on Anthropic's most advanced AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: Prominent cybersecurity leaders — including CISOs, security researchers and executives at Adobe, Zoom and Sophos — are urging the Trump administration to reverse restrictions on Anthropic's most advanced AI models, arguing the move hurts cyber defenders more than attackers.

key_facts.fact: The loosely organized group, led by former Facebook CSO Alex Stamos, argues in the letter that the issue Amazon researchers flagged exists across other leading AI models too.
key_facts.excerpt: The loosely organized group of experts, led by former Facebook Chief Security Officer Alex Stamos, argue in the letter that the issue Amazon researchers flagged exists across other leading AI models, too.

key_facts.fact: As of Sunday evening, the letter had over 40 signatories, including Luta Security CEO Katie Moussouris, SocialProof Security CEO Rachel Tobac, Veracode co-founder Chris Wysopal, computer scientist Paul Vixie, Sophos CEO Joe Levy and Nvidia security researcher Aaron Grattafiori.
key_facts.excerpt: As of Sunday evening, the letter had over 40 signatories. Luta Security CEO Katie Moussouris, SocialProof Security CEO Rachel Tobac, Veracode co-founder Chris Wysopal, prominent computer scientist Paul Vixie, Sophos CEO Joe Levy and Nvidia security researcher Aaron Grattafiori are among those who signed the letter.

key_facts.fact: The letter argues the action 'has taken the best models away from defenders, created market uncertainty, and risked America's AI leadership without any real risk to justify it.'
key_facts.excerpt: "This action has taken the best models away from defenders, created market uncertainty, and risked America's AI leadership without any real risk to justify it," the letter says.

key_facts.fact: Stamos, now chief product officer at Corridor, told Axios that the Fable 5 capability that alarmed the White House was the model's ability to create a 'proof of concept' for vulnerabilities; only Mythos 5 and Mythos Preview, available to Project Glasswing members, could turn those into fully autonomous attack chains.
key_facts.excerpt: Stamos, now the chief product officer at Corridor, told Axios that the Fable 5 security capabilities that appeared to alarm the White House was the model's ability to create a 'proof of concept' for vulnerabilities. Only Mythos 5 and Mythos Preview — which had been available only to vetted members of Anthropic's Project Glasswing initiative before Friday — could turn those proofs of concept into fully autonomous attack chains, Stamos said.

sources.title: Alex Stamos, cybersecurity leaders push Trump to restore Anthropic Mythos and Fable access

stories.headline: Canadian PM Carney and EU warn US Anthropic ban shows risks of AI over-reliance and lack of tech sovereignty

key_facts.fact: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said the US Anthropic ban shows the dangers of 'over-reliance on certain models', and compared the risks to those that led to the 2008 financial crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: Canadian PM says the Anthropic ban shows the dangers of 'over-reliance on certain models', and compares the risks to those that led to the 2008 financial crisis

key_facts.fact: The European Commission says it is looking at the practical consequences of US restrictions on Anthropic's models, noting such measures 'should not be discriminatory against partners'.
key_facts.excerpt: EU says it is looking at the practical consequences of US restricting Anthropic's models, notes such measures 'should not be discriminatory against partners'

key_facts.fact: EU officials called the Anthropic decision a 'further illustration' of why Europe needs stronger tech sovereignty.
key_facts.excerpt: JUST IN: EU says the Anthropic decision is a 'further illustration' of why Europe needs stronger tech sovereignty.

key_facts.fact: Former Trump administration AI advisor Dean Ball called the move 'baffling', pointing to inconsistency between loosening chip export controls to China and a blanket restriction on access to Anthropic models for all foreign governments, including close allies that had been relying on Mythos to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities in critical systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Former Trump administration AI advisor Dean Ball called the move 'baffling,' pointing to the apparent inconsistency between the administration's willingness to loosen export controls on advanced chips to China and the blanket restriction on access to Anthropic's advanced models for all foreign governments, including close allies, many of whom were already relying on Mythos to identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities in critical systems.

stories.headline: Apple's new Siri AI 'good enough' to ease its AI crisis; iOS 27 builds include third-party AI model support beyond OpenAI

key_facts.fact: Mark Gurman, in a Power On column published June 14, writes that Apple's new Siri AI, while mainly delivering the basics, is 'good enough' to pull Apple out of its AI crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: Power On: Apple's new Siri AI is just good enough to pull it out of its AI crisis. My hands-on impressions of the new assistant and AI features.

key_facts.fact: Sources tell Gurman that the ability to tap third-party AI models beyond OpenAI's is already active in internal iOS 27 builds.
key_facts.excerpt: Siri AI is good enough to ease Apple's AI crisis; sources: the ability to tap third party AI models beyond OpenAI's is already active in internal iOS 27 builds

key_facts.fact: Gurman frames the user-facing tradeoff as 'Siri AI is like iMovie and ChatGPT is like Final Cut Pro' — Siri AI can handle the basics, but power users will want third-party AI for extra functionality.
key_facts.excerpt: For those in the Mac world, Siri AI is like iMovie and ChatGPT is like Final Cut Pro. Siri AI can handle the basics — and a bit more — but power users will want the extra functionality.

key_facts.fact: Gurman writes that 'the new Siri finally works as it is supposed to for the first time in 15 years' and that its pre-installed status will give Apple a competitive baseline to ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude.
key_facts.excerpt: The new Siri finally works as it is supposed to for the first time in 15 years and the pre-installed status is going to give Apple a competitive baseline to ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude that will steal

key_facts.fact: Gurman expects Apple to eventually build its own 'OpenClaw competitor' that could fully operate its software across iPhones, iPads and Macs on behalf of the user.
key_facts.excerpt: Longer term, I'd also expect Apple to try to create its own OpenClaw competitor, delivering a system that could fully operate its software across iPhones, iPads and Macs on behalf of the user.

key_facts.fact: The Verge notes the new Siri is built on Gemini models, which is consistent with Apple's reported partnership with Google for Siri AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: New Siri is built on Gemini models, so it makes a lot of sense that the first iteration of Siri AI feels a little bit 'Gemini, circa 2025.'

sources.title: Power On: Apple's New Siri AI Is Just Good Enough to Save Apple's AI Crisis

stories.headline: Tencent-backed Enflame wins STAR Market IPO approval to raise ~$830M as last of China's four leading AI chipmakers

key_facts.fact: Shanghai Enflame Technology Co., backed by Tencent, has received approval for an initial public offering on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market, becoming the last of China's four leading AI chipmakers to go to market.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent-backed Enflame receives approval for a Shanghai IPO and plans to raise ~$888M; Enflame is the last of China's four leading AI chipmakers to go to market

key_facts.fact: Enflame is targeting a raise of approximately RMB 6 billion (~$830 million) on the STAR Market.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is targeting a raise of approximately RMB 6 billion, roughly $830 million, to fund the development and mass production of its next-generation AI semiconductors.

key_facts.fact: Tencent holds 20.26% of Enflame and accounted for 71.84% of its revenue, making it both the company's largest shareholder and dominant customer.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent is simultaneously Enflame's biggest backer, its largest shareholder, and the source of nearly three quarters of its revenue.

key_facts.fact: Enflame, founded in March 2018, has self-iterated four generations of architecture and five cloud AI chips, with cumulative losses of RMB 4.29 billion (~$600M) over three years.
key_facts.excerpt: Enflame's financials reveal challenges, including cumulative losses of RMB 4.29 billion($600 million) over three years and a heavy reliance on Tencent, its largest customer and shareholder.

key_facts.fact: IPO proceeds are earmarked for fifth- and sixth-generation AI chip products, expected to debut in 2027 and 2029, rather than expansion of current deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: The IPO proceeds are earmarked for research and development plus industrialization of Enflame's fifth and sixth-generation AI chip series. Those products are expected to debut in 2027 and 2029, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Chinese regulators eased listing rules for unprofitable hardware companies in June 2025, and rivals Moore Threads, MetaX and Biren have already gone public and are trading above IPO prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese regulators eased listing rules for unprofitable hardware companies in June 2025, which is partly why Enflame can pursue this listing at all despite its loss profile. Moore Threads, MetaX, and Biren have already gone public and are trading well above their IPO prices.

stories.headline: ByteDance in talks for at least 50,000 Iluvatar CoreX inference chips, also weighing Baidu's Kunlunxin

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is in talks with Shanghai-based Iluvatar CoreX to purchase AI chips for inference work and is also considering a similar deal with Baidu, according to two sources familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese technology company ByteDance is in talks with Shanghai-based Iluvatar CoreX to purchase AI chips for inference work and is also considering a similar deal with Baidu, according to two sources familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Iluvatar CoreX is expected to ship at least 50,000 chips to ByteDance this year, most of them for inference workloads as ByteDance widens the user base of Doubao, its consumer chatbot.
key_facts.excerpt: Iluvatar CoreX is expected to ship at least 50,000 chips to ByteDance this year, the sources said, most of them destined for inference work rather than training. Inference, the business of answering user queries once a model is built, is the less hardware-hungry half of the AI workload, and it is where Chinese designers have the better chance of matching imported silicon. ByteDance wants the capacity to widen the user base of Doubao, its consumer chatbot.

key_facts.fact: If a deal is reached, Iluvatar CoreX would become ByteDance's third major domestic GPU supplier after Huawei and Cambricon; a Baidu Kunlunxin deal would make it a fourth.
key_facts.excerpt: Should a deal be agreed, Iluvatar would become ByteDance's third major domestic GPU supplier, after Huawei and Cambricon. The company is also weighing a separate purchase of Baidu's Kunlunxin chips, the same people said, which would give it a fourth.

key_facts.fact: Iluvatar's flagship TianGai-100 line is positioned as a domestic alternative to Nvidia's A100; until recently the company sold almost entirely to government buyers.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance is in talks to buy artificial-intelligence chips from Iluvatar CoreX, a Shanghai-based GPU maker that until recently sold almost entirely to government buyers, according to people familiar with the discussions cited by Reuters.

key_facts.fact: ByteDance has also been developing its own custom AI silicon and was reportedly in talks with Samsung as recently as February 2026 about potential manufacturing partnerships, giving it three parallel tracks.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance has also been developing its own custom AI silicon and was reportedly in talks with Samsung as recently as February 2026 about potential manufacturing partnerships. That's three parallel tracks: buy from Iluvatar, buy from Baidu's chip unit, and build your own.

stories.headline: Madrid-based Orbio raises $21M Series A led by Dawn Capital to automate hiring and onboarding for frontline workers

key_facts.fact: Orbio announced a $21 million Series A on Monday, June 14, in a round led by Dawn Capital.
key_facts.excerpt: On Monday, the company announced a $21 million Series A in a round led by Dawn Capital.

key_facts.fact: Orbio's customers already include Poke and YUM! Brands (owners of Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and KFC), which use the platform to onboard and manage frontline employees.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup says its customers already include Poke and YUM! Brands (owners of Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, and KFC), to onboard and manage their frontline employees.

key_facts.fact: Orbio's AI agents — named Maria, Daniel and Claire — can interview candidates, assess fit, monitor employee output and conduct daily check-ins throughout an employee's work lifecycle.
key_facts.excerpt: The Orbio agents (Maria, Daniel, and Claire) can interview candidates, assess fit, monitor employee output, and conduct daily check-ins throughout an employee's work lifecycle.

key_facts.fact: At behavioral health provider The Stepping Stones Group, Orbio now runs the company's full US operation, with 20% more candidates making it through to hire.
key_facts.excerpt: As an example, he said that at behavioral health provider The Stepping Stones Group, Orbio now runs the company's full US operation, with 20% more candidates making it through to get hired

key_facts.fact: The platform reaches deskless workers through WhatsApp and phone calls, with no corporate login or email required, and Orbio's agents have been trained on millions of frontline conversations in healthcare, hospitality and logistics.
key_facts.excerpt: The platform uses AI agents through WhatsApp and phone calls, so no corporate login or email is needed. Candidates can apply, get a response in seconds, complete an AI-led interview, and start onboarding the same day.

key_facts.fact: Orbio has raised about $26-28 million to date from investors including Visionaries, 2100 Ventures, Plus Partners and Enzo Ventures, with founders previously having sold startups Cobee and Nucoro.
key_facts.excerpt: Dawn Capital, a London-based B2B software investor managing $2 billion, led the Series A round. Visionaries VC, Plus Partners, and Enzo Ventures also continued their support. Since launching in June 2025, Orbio has raised about $28 million in total.
